newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity regulator may cut bills -paper.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity regulator may cut bills -paper.

text.p: UK electricity bills could fall by 10 percent next year because of fresh price controls being considered by the industry regulator ahead of the introduction of a competitive market in household power, the Times said on Friday.
The paper said issue was raised by Stephen Littlechild, the industry regulator, in the latest round of his review into the pricing restraints that operate on the supply side of electricity.

Prospects of price cuts next year come as fears circulate among consumer groups that the companies will seek to pass on the bills for windfall tax through prices by trying to negotiate leniency in pricing reviews, the paper said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
